PullRequest.Title: test: simplify editor tabs fixture coverage
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up fixture cleanup to #340635. Organize the editor tabs gallery around the intended Density, Layout, and Styles coverage without changing production styling or retained scenes.

- Remove the Colors group and its unused custom-color, stylesheet, and editor-frame helpers.
- Keep Light and Dark for Density and Layout; keep the additional Light High Contrast and Dark High Contrast variants only for Styles.
- Retain the existing scene implementations and reusable tabs renderer used by Sessions fixtures.
- Update existing Playwright checks to use the retained Styles high-contrast scenes. Remove checks exclusive to retired customization, DarkModern, and single-tab high-contrast scenes.

## Testing

1. Open the component gallery and inspect `editor/tabs`: Density contains Default and Compact, Layout retains its existing scenarios, and Styles contains Connected, Legacy, and Pill. Colors and DarkModern variants are absent.
2. Compare the retained Light and Dark scenes, plus the Styles high-contrast scenes, with the pre-cleanup gallery. Their screenshots are byte-for-byte unchanged.
3. Render the Sessions editor-header and grid fixtures that use the shared tabs renderer, including high-contrast variants.

Local validation passed:

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/editor/tabs.fixture.ts`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run eslint -- test/componentFixtures/playwright/tests/editorTabBar.spec.ts`
- `npm --prefix test/componentFixtures/playwright test -- tests/editorTabBar.spec.ts --workers 1` — passed; retained border and action hover/focus checks navigate to existing fixtures.
- `./node_modules/.bin/component-explorer render --project test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --fixture-id-regex '^editor/tabs/' --target <evidence-directory>/cleaned --useHashPaths --workers 1`
- Temporary probes using the existing Rspack rendering API checked the exact tree and themes, preserved image hashes and PNG bytes, immediate and delayed screenshots, remounts, and teardown for the retained scenes and shared Sessions consumers.
- Independent local code review and Copilot CLI review found no actionable defects.

This is fixture-only cleanup, not a functional bug fix. The PR remains draft pending the coordinated combined-regression gate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or batch-rendering the editor/tabs component gallery across Density, Layout, and Styles theme variants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture registration determines the available variants; selecting a variant synchronously creates the in-memory editor model and DOM, sets the existing theme, opens tabs, and lays out the title control before the fixture is ready. Wrapped layouts may wait for animation frames to stabilize. The diff removes custom-theme cloning, stylesheet adoption, whole fixture groups, and extra theme variants rather than adding work to this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of fixture/theme variants selected for rendering and, within a fixture, the bounded editor-tab count. Both effective variant cardinality and custom stylesheet work decrease.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each fixture render is synchronous within its browser context; wrapped stabilization is serialized across at most 10 animation frames. External batch renderers can use workers, but this diff reduces the number of independent fixture variants available to schedule.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme variants are materialized by the fixture framework and the shared test theme service receives the selected existing theme. The removed custom-color fixtures previously created unique theme IDs and per-render stylesheets; retained fixtures introduce no new cache keys, misses, or retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff and fixture framework directly show fewer variants and removal of theme cloning and adopted stylesheet lifecycle work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact batch-render savings depend on whether callers render the full gallery or one selected fixture, but no changed retained route performs more work than before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Gallery startup/registration and batch capture have less work, while retained scene render paths preserve the same bounded model and DOM construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running editorTabBar Playwright checks against retained dark and high-contrast scenes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each test performs one localhost page navigation, waits for the selected fixture to render, then reads computed styles or drives hover/focus. Navigation and fixture rendering are on the test critical path. The altered high-contrast checks still perform one navigation each; many other tests and navigations are deleted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Playwright page.goto loads the component explorer fixture from the local web server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one localhost navigation per test invocation. The retained tests whose fixture IDs changed still issue one navigation each; the PR deletes numerous tests, reducing total suite navigation cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, each corresponding retained check also called openFixture once, while the removed tests each added another localhost navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The page load must complete before each test can inspect the fixture.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Aggregate work scales with test count under the configured worker pool. This PR sharply lowers test count; retained per-test fixture cardinality remains a small fixed number of tabs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Playwright configuration uses fullyParallel=true, so independent tests may run concurrently up to the runner's worker count; each individual test serializes its single navigation and interactions. Deleting tests reduces, rather than increases, the aggregate browser/network burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All navigations target the same local built explorer and may benefit from browser HTTP caching, but each page still mounts the requested fixture. Changed fixture IDs reuse existing Styles scenes; no new cache namespace or miss loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for navigation cardinality and full parallel scheduling, based on openFixture and Playwright configuration; low magnitude concern for the bounded scene complexity change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact CI duration reduction depends on worker count and cache warmth. The two outline tests now mount the default multi-tab Styles scene instead of a single-tab Density scene, but the extra bounded tabs are too small to establish a meaningful regression and total suite work falls substantially.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The same one-navigation boundary remains for altered tests, while deletion of many checks lowers total browser, network, layout, and computed-style work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering shared Sessions editor-header and grid fixtures through renderEditorTabsFixture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sessions fixtures call renderEditorTabsFixture synchronously to construct their tab model and DOM before their containing fixture can render. The searched callers pass neither removed colorCustomizations nor editorFrame, so they continue to set the supplied context theme and execute the same title-control layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the bounded number of rendered Sessions panes and tabs; the diff does not change either effective cardinality or per-pane work for these consumers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each shared renderer invocation completes synchronously during its fixture mount. A composite Sessions scene may invoke it for a bounded number of panes, with no changed queue, limiter, or parallel boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Callers continue to use the context's existing theme and shared TestThemeService. They never generated customized theme IDs or adopted per-render stylesheets, so warm and cold behavior is unchanged by the removed customization branch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository-wide symbol search found the three external call sites, and their option objects do not use either removed capability.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Composite fixture pane counts vary by Sessions scene, but all searched call sites omit the removed options, making their before/after work equivalent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Shared consumers follow the unchanged branch and gain no new allocation, layout, I/O, or retained-state cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The PR is fixture/test cleanup: it removes custom theme/style lifecycle work, fixture variants, tests, and page loads. Retained gallery, Playwright, and Sessions paths add no concrete scaling, boundary, concurrency, cache, layout, or retention regression, so no findings were submitted.
